analyst.summary: Paytm has posted four consecutive profitable quarters (Q1 FY26 Rs123cr through Q1 FY27 Rs220cr, the latter reported 20-Jul-2026), with FY26 revenue of Rs8,437cr (+22%) and PAT of Rs552cr reversing a Rs663cr FY25 loss -- though FY26 revenue is still below the FY24 pre-PPBL-disruption peak of Rs9,978cr, so part of the growth is base-effect recovery, moderating each quarter (Q1 FY27 +28%/+31% ex-incentives). Merchant GMV (+31% YoY to Rs7.1 lakh cr), net payment margin (>4bps, structurally improving), device subscriptions (1.6cr merchants, +21% YoY) and financial-services revenue (+45% YoY to Rs814cr, on recovering lending-partner volumes and >50% repeat-borrower disbursals) all point to a genuine, multi-quarter operational recovery from the 2024 RBI/PPBL disruption, not a one-off print. FY26's PAT is not inflated by one-off gains -- exceptional items were a net loss for the year -- but a large share of quarterly PAT still overlaps with ~Rs750-900cr/year of treasury/interest income from the Dec-2024 PayPay stake-sale proceeds (Rs13,315cr cash pile), which management guides is already declining (rate cuts, and a proposed Rs1,686cr reallocation of IPO proceeds to shareholders) -- so PAT durability increasingly depends on core EBITDA (still only 7-8% margin) rather than the treasury cushion. RBI cancelled PPBL's banking licence effective 24-Apr-2026, but One97's PPBL investment was already fully impaired since Mar-2024, and the market/brokerages treated it as an already-priced-in, non-operational event, confirmed by an unaffected Q1 FY27 print. At ~Rs86,364cr market cap (~133x TTM PAT of ~Rs649cr), the stock is priced for continued high growth plus material EBITDA-margin expansion -- a defensible-but-unproven bet given four straight quarters of genuine delivery. No quant score exists yet for this name; per the V1 asymmetric-override rule the call defaults to Hold.
